endorsements.quote: Known best practices for monitoring AI include scheduled review of AI algorithm content and performance, monitoring data inputs, identifying drift, and assessing key performance indicators.
When implementing AI to reduce clinicians’ cognitive burden, health systems and vendors should measure and monitor key performance indicators.
AI tools must be well-implemented and monitored for unintended consequences to optimize their benefits.
As healthcare examines and segments various sources of data to identify bias, it will be necessary to continue to monitor those metrics after AI implementation.
Ultimately, it is important to have transparency about what the algorithm includes and publish results and performance metrics.

unlisted_practices: Engage frontline clinical staff and other end users in the design and implementation of AI tools using user-centered design.
Measure cognitive load and workload at baseline and at multiple points in the AI development life cycle, preferring non-obtrusive metrics such as EHR event log data.
Do not use AI primarily to justify staff reductions; measure return on investment and impact on staff rather than focusing only on cost savings.
Design AI implementation for sustainability from the start and empower local stakeholders to plan, measure, and refine the practice.
Build multiple models, such as with and without demographic variables, to better understand potential bias in algorithms.
Conduct rigorous cross-site evaluation of EHR vendor AI functionality that reduces cognitive and work burden, and publish and share results widely.
Provide clinicians with appropriate product labeling and methodology disclosures from AI developers.

screen.reason: Perspective/call-to-action outlining critical issues and recommendations for vendors and health systems deploying AI to reduce clinician burden and monitor bias.
